claim:
Let \(X=\ell_2-\ell_\infty\) be the real Day--James plane
\[
\|(s,t)\|_{2,\infty}=
\begin{cases}
\sqrt{s^2+t^2},&st\ge0,\\
\max\{|s|,|t|\},&st\le0.
\end{cases}
\]
Its Dunkl--Williams constant is the known value \(DW(X)=2\sqrt2\), but the defining supremum is not attained: there are no nonzero distinct \(x,y\in X\) for which
\[
\frac{\|x\|+\|y\|}{\|x-y\|}
\left\|\frac{x}{\|x\|}-\frac{y}{\|y\|}\right\|
=2\sqrt2.
\]
Equivalently, in the unit-sphere formula
\[
DW(X)=
\sup_{\substack{u,v\in S_X\\u+v\ne0}}
\frac{\|u+v\|}
{\min_{0\le t\le1}\|(1-t)u+tv\|},
\]
every admissible quotient is strictly smaller than \(2\sqrt2\), although an explicit sequence of such quotients converges to \(2\sqrt2\).
integrity: The proof reconstructs the complete extreme-point reduction and strict branch bounds from the accessible 2013 full text, checks the remaining endpoints directly, and uses an exact symbolic sharp sequence. No numerical experiment is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: Specific to the real Day--James plane ell_2-ell_infinity. The result proves nonattainment and gives one exact maximizing sequence, but does not classify every maximizing sequence.
title: Nonattainment of the Dunkl--Williams constant in the Day--James Euclidean--sup plane
